description:
Goal
Remove telemetry ownership from semantic World so World is an owned, lifetime-free authority that synchronous handlers can borrow directly.

Current state
World with lifetime parameter `a` stores &\x27a dyn Telemetry. This couples every semantic API to observer lifetime, prevents World from satisfying Any, encourages emit sites to flatten World state into metadata, and prevents a statically owned NullTelemetry specialization at the Compiler2 boundary. The explicit World lifetime surface spans 26 production files; the migration is necessarily atomic because owning both World and telemetry while World borrows telemetry would be self-referential, while partial compatibility scaffolding would preserve the wrong boundary.

Proven shape
The spike established that the viable ownership model is:
- lifetime-free World containing semantic state only;
- Compiler2<T: Telemetry> owning World and T separately;
- a short-lived execution context reborrowing &mut World and &T only while an operation requires both;
- mutation completed before handlers receive immutable raw authority references.
Baseline spike gates passed cargo check --lib, World tests 19/19, compiler2 front-door tests 12/12, product-drive tests 11/11, and telemetry-dump tests 4/4 with 2 ignored. The prototype is deliberately uncommitted until the atomic migration is fully green.

Strategy
- Make World contain semantic state only.
- Make Compiler2<T> own World and the telemetry implementation separately.
- Introduce a short-lived execution/job context that reborrows &mut World and &T for operations requiring both.
- Keep state mutation in World and expose the existing decision result. After mutable borrows end, emit an immutable &World plus raw decision-local references.
- Jobs::run receives the context; pure helpers continue to receive World.
- Product producers split world/telemetry borrows; dump emitters take (&World, telemetry).
- Destructure context fields before opening spans or ProductDriver and end mutable store borrows before emitting immutable World.
- Do not introduce Rc into World, global telemetry, unsafe lifetime erasure, a self-referential owner, Deref-based context forwarding, a World facade duplicating state, or compatibility forwarding methods.

TDD
Add compile-time/type tests showing World has no lifetime or telemetry field and can be borrowed as an opaque event-scoped value. Preserve semantic behavior, event ordering, and the existing focused front-door/product/telemetry contracts through the ownership-only move.

Acceptance
- World is lifetime-free and telemetry-free.
- Compiler2 can own NullTelemetry or configured telemetry alongside World.
- Jobs receive telemetry only through the short-lived execution context.
- Handlers can borrow immutable World only after mutation borrows end.
- Existing behavior and telemetry ordering remain green before payload/API migration.
- Docs describe authority and observer ownership; full library tests and clippy pass warning-free.

Audit-required corrections
The first implementation commit bcb874441 failed architectural audit despite green gates and must not be folded as-is.
- ExecutionContext erased Compiler2<T> immediately to &dyn Telemetry, and jobs/World mutation methods propagated dynamic dispatch. This defeats the owned NullTelemetry specialization and would require another whole-tree migration before no-handler telemetry can be statically stripped. Preserve T through ExecutionContext and every emit-bearing call path; do not erase at the compiler boundary.
- activation_inputs.defined exposed an immutable World after updating the activation store but before work_graph.complete published the corresponding fact. A handler therefore observed a split state while docs called it post-mutation authority. Emit authority-bearing events only after all stores/facts comprising the decision have been updated, and test the authority visible at that exact event.
- Align fact-engine documentation with the actual owner of post-application emission.

comments.text: SPIKE PROOF: target is viable; no prototype commit because a partial migration would knowingly not compile or would drop observations. World becomes lifetime-free semantic state; Compiler2<T: Telemetry> owns World+T; short-lived ExecutionContext holds split &mut World and &dyn Telemetry. Explicit World lifetime surface is 26 production files; 213 World::new(&tel) and 566 Compiler2::new(&tel) call sites. Move drive/complete_job/warning emission to Context; jobs::run takes Context; pure helpers remain World; product producers split world/tel; dump emitters take (&World, tel); lowerers take Context only if they emit. Critical borrow rule: destructure Context fields before opening spans/ProductDriver; end mutable store borrows before emitting immutable &World. Do not Deref Context to World, add a forwarding facade, unsafe erase lifetimes, or store Rc telemetry in World. Atomicity confirmed: owning World+telemetry while World borrows telemetry is self-referential, and splitting into independently green commits would require forbidden scaffolding. Spike baseline checks: cargo check --lib; world 19/19; compiler2 front door 12/12; product_drive 11/11; telemetry_dump 4/4 (2 ignored).

title: Remove telemetry ownership and lifetime from World
